unintendedEffects.description: Phase A drain of the DOLA and USDC legs depends on a chain of LIVE external oracles being fresh at execution time: the AutoDOLA and AutoUSDC vaults are Tokemak AutopoolETH proxies whose redeem path prices the underlying via CurveConvexDestinationVaultV2.getUnderlyerFloorPrice -> CustomSetOracle (InvalidAge ceiling ~89496s) and RootPriceOracle (Chainlink ETH/USD staleness). If totalWithdrawal is broadcast while any of these is stale, the redeem reverts and Phase A aborts the whole single-broadcast migration.
unintendedEffects.why-unintended: The script's stated purpose is a deterministic owner-gated cutover; it has no awareness of, retry around, or pre-check for the third-party oracle freshness that the redeem transitively requires. The 24-72h execution window does NOT guarantee oracle freshness inside it.
unintendedEffects.verified: fork-preview (InvalidAge(89496) on DOLA, 0x8d54ba1f Chainlink on tighter warp); USDe (no oracle dep) drained cleanly to prove the contrast

unintendedEffects.description: Re-deposited principal == actual vault redeem proceeds, which can be LESS than the snapshot principal (USDe E2E: snapshot 3763.927 USDe, received 3762.379 -> minter's recorded backing principal drops by ~1.55 USDe per leg). The exchangeRate is preserved at 1e18, so the minter's accounted collateral is marginally reduced. This is the documented 'use actual received' behaviour (ERC4626 redeem rounding/cost) and is correct, but it is a real reduction in the minter's recorded principal that is neither asserted nor logged-with-tolerance.
unintendedEffects.why-unintended: Not a clobber of unrelated state, but a state change (reduced minter principal) beyond the literal 'preserve' framing in the NatSpec.
